countries.name: Fiji
countries.summary: Fiji is a Pacific Island nation with English-medium medical education tracing back over a century, offering direct-entry MBBS programmes recognized in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools and drawing students from across the Pacific region and beyond.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: Fiji offers an English-medium, direct-entry MBBS with WHO/FAIMER recognition, clinical training at named regional hospitals, and a compact island setting, appealing to students seeking a Pacific-region medical education outside the more commonly chosen European or South Asian destinations.
countries.climate: Tropical maritime climate, warm year-round with a wetter season from November to April and a drier season from May to October.

countries.metaDescription: Explore English-medium MBBS programs in Fiji, including admissions, fees, recognition and clinical training guidance for international students.

universities.name: University of Fiji, Umanand Prasad School of Medicine and Health Sciences
universities.summary: University of Fiji's Umanand Prasad School of Medicine and Health Sciences has run its MBBS programme since 2008 across campuses in Lautoka and Suva. The programme is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 2011 onward, degrees are noted as acceptable to Canadian provincial and territorial medical regulators, and the university is registered with Fiji's Higher Education Commission.
universities.campusLifestyle: MBBS is taught across two campuses: Saweni (Lautoka, the original site) and Samabula (Suva, added in 2017). The programme runs 32 courses over 720 credit points across six years, with clinical practice incorporated from the start of the course.
universities.cityProfile: Lautoka is Fiji's second-largest city, on the western side of the main island of Viti Levu; Suva, the capital, hosts the university's second MBBS campus. Both cities give students access to major public hospital networks for clinical training.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year MBBS runs preclinical foundations (anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, medical ethics) in Years 1-2, then clinical rotation blocks of decreasing length across Years 3-6, covering internal medicine, general surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, community health and family medicine, psychiatry, and forensic medicine, concluding with an Objective Structured Clinical Examination in Year 6. Clinical training is anchored at Colonial War Memorial Hospital in Suva, and since an April 2025 memorandum of understanding, at Pacific Specialist Healthcare in Nadi for advanced and specialist attachments including cardiology and neurosurgery, plus telemedicine training. Graduates undergo a compulsory rotating internship, extended from one to two years under a 2020 Fiji Ministry of Health policy update, before registering to practise with the Fiji Medical and Dental Council.
universities.hostelOverview: No public dormitory fee schedule or dedicated international-student housing page was found on the university's official site; the university does have an Accommodation Officer role on staff, confirming some administrative accommodation function exists. Applicants should contact the university's admissions office directly to confirm current housing options before enrolling.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published. Food costs should be planned as part of an independent living-cost budget.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. The university's regulations reference district-based accommodation falling under its Finance, Planning and Development division.
universities.studentSupport: International applications are reviewed case-by-case by the university's Student Academic Services team (admissions@unifiji.ac.fj), and a documented Tuition Fee Waiver Policy covers specific hardship circumstances, including for a student who has been refused a study permit.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0002639), currently operational, with ECFMG-certification eligibility for graduates from 2011 onward and Canadian medical-regulator acceptability noted in the same record.
Registered with Fiji's Higher Education Commission, with the MBBS explicitly listed as a recognized provider qualification.

A recently formalized (April 2025) clinical partnership with Pacific Specialist Healthcare in Nadi, adding advanced specialist training in cardiology and neurosurgery alongside the established Colonial War Memorial Hospital placement.
A published, dated, official fee schedule with a clear, documented refund and withdrawal policy.
A documented tuition fee waiver for international students who are refused a study permit, an unusual and useful applicant protection.
thingsToConsider: No fixed application deadline is published; the university states international applications are decided on a case-by-case, effectively rolling basis, so applicants should apply well ahead of the intake they want.
There is no online application portal; applications go by a downloadable PDF form submitted by email or post, not through a modern online system.

The university's own MBBS page still describes a one-year post-graduation internship, but Fiji's Ministry of Health updated this to a two-year rotating internship in 2020; the longer, more current figure should be assumed.
The official fee schedule does not disclose the rate for Australian or New Zealand citizens, only a combined 'other countries' international rate double the domestic rate.
Indian applicants must separately satisfy India's National Medical Commission NEET-UG Eligibility Certificate requirement; this is not referenced or administered by the university.
bestFitFor: Students who meet the university's direct-entry academic threshold (roughly 320/400 marks with strong English, Biology and Mathematics grades) and are comfortable with a paper-based, case-by-case international application process.
Applicants interested in Pacific-region clinical training and the university's growing specialist-hospital partnership network.
Families able to budget for a substantial six-year tuition total and plan independently for accommodation, given the limited published housing information.

faq.question: Is the MBBS programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. The primary route is Direct Entry from Fiji Year 13 (FSFE) or an equivalent secondary qualification, with no separate bachelor's stage required first.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS), followed by a compulsory rotating internship (two years, per Fiji's Ministry of Health) before registering with the Fiji Medical and Dental Council.

faq.question: How long is the programme and how is it structured?
faq.answer: Six years (720 credit points across 32 courses): preclinical foundations in Years 1-2, then clinical rotation blocks of decreasing length through Years 3-6, concluding with an Objective Structured Clinical Examination.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: For international students (outside Fiji, the Pacific Islands Forum, Australia and New Zealand), the official 2026 fee schedule lists FJD 34,760 per year in Years 1-3, FJD 35,860 in Years 4-5, and FJD 36,960 in Year 6, for a total of roughly FJD 212,960 across the programme.

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: There is no standalone entrance exam. Direct-entry applicants need an aggregate of at least 320 out of 400 marks across four subjects (English, Biology and Mathematics compulsory, plus Chemistry, Physics or Computer Science), with a minimum of 60% in English. International applicants are additionally assessed case-by-case with a recent medical report and evidence of English proficiency.

faq.question: How do I apply, and when does the academic year start?
faq.answer: There is no online application portal; applicants complete a downloadable PDF application form and submit it by email or post. No fixed international application deadline is published -- decisions are made case-by-case. Semester 1 begins in mid-February and Semester 2 in mid-to-late July.

faq.question: Is a scholarship available for international MBBS students?
faq.answer: No scholarship specifically for international MBBS students was found. The university's loan and scholarship schemes (the UniFiji Loan Scheme and Tertiary Scholarship and Loans Board programmes) are oriented toward Fiji citizens.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

programmes.officialTitle: Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS)

fee.notes: Officially published 2026 tuition for international students (Column B, 'Citizens of Other Countries, except Australia and New Zealand'): FJD 34,760/year in Years 1-3, FJD 35,860/year in Years 4-5, and FJD 36,960 in Year 6, totalling approximately FJD 212,960 across the six-year programme, per the university's official 2026 Fee Structure document. This rate is exactly double the domestic Fiji/Pacific-Islands-Forum-citizen rate. The Australia/New Zealand citizen rate is not disclosed in this document. Refund policy: full refund if formally withdrawn by the second Friday of the semester, with a 25% weekly penalty thereafter and no refund after the fifth Friday. A tuition fee waiver is available for, among other grounds, an international student who has been refused a study permit.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants with a secondary-education qualification equivalent to Fiji Year 13 (FSFE), assessed case-by-case, meeting an aggregate of at least 320/400 marks with strong English, Biology and Mathematics grades
restrictions: International candidates are decided on a case-by-case basis and must submit a recent (within 3 months) medical report plus evidence of English proficiency, though no specific minimum test score is published
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: The university's general Admissions Regulations page states a lower entry bar (300/400 marks, 50% English) than the MBBS-specific programme page and 2026 Handbook (320/400, 60% English) -- the more specific, more recently dated MBBS/Handbook figures are treated as authoritative.
